151.19: Then O fair-complexioned lady, the Kasthlla spoke to me in human voice. She addressed me by my name Sandhya- vail, while I was in the midst of my friends.
151.20: "O splendid-faced lady in my previous birth I was the daughter of the sage named Sumantu who was omni¬ scient. I was the wife of Kauntfinya.
151.21: I lived in Kanyakubja (Kanauj in U.P.). I was affluent, hence, very arrogant. I was the favourite darling of my mother, father and other kinsmen.
151.22: Bed and other things were given to me by my father as dowry and present. Ten thousand gold pieces too were given to me at the outset by my father-in-law.
151.23: Taking the dead body of her husband my mother-in- law entered the funeral pyre. Thereafter, my husband offered water libations to his parents and performed their Sraddha.
151.24: Within two months of that, O gentle lady, my husband went to the Royal palace out of curiosity but was afterwards overwhelmed by love passions of the heart.
151.25: Beautiful courtesans in the prime of their youth were seen entering the royal palace by that Brahmana.
151.26: With gifts of profuse wealth two of them were taken from there and brought to his house. My evil-minded husband retained them in his house for dalliance.
151.27: Using it up the entire wealth of my husband was wasted by both of them. O gentle lady, by the time three years elapsed, my husband became indigent.
151.28: Then he requested me "Give me your ornaments". Those were not given to my husband by me as he was addicted to vice.
151.29: He went a long distance seeing wonderful things and miracles on the way. O splendid lady, he saw many animals of the sea and all their activities.
151.30: By the time it had gone a hundred Yojanas, the boat was caught in a violent storm. It broke into pieces and all others on the boat were killed.
151.31: As providence would have it, and urged by his Karmans of the previous births, my husband clung to along piece of wood. O gentle lady, led by the wind he reached a mountain bedecked with adamantine peaks.
151.32: O lady of beautiful eyes, on seeing the divine, wonderfnl mountain my husbund left off the piece of wood (that brought him there) and jocously climbed on to it, as he was eager to earn some wealth.
151.33: He rested there for a while. When he was over- whelmed with hunger and thirst, he got up in search of food
151.34: When the sun had set and the night had set in, a terrible Raksasa roaring like the cloud came there rushing in.
151.35: Without washing her feet, she had gone to sleep with her head directed towards the north. The virgin of beautiful buttocks was desirous of obtaining a husband, but did not obtain one befitting her,
151.36: O lady of slender limbs, this beautiful girl, occupying a bed spread in the shadow of the lamp was seen by the sin¬ ful demon who was roaming about.
151.37: On hearing the weeping of the girl, his wife the ogress hurriedly came to the place where the demon was standing.
151.38: "O ruthless one, why is this girl brought here when I am alive? Do you wish for another wife? I will no longer be your wife then.
151.39: That demon joyously spoke to his beloved wife of beautiful eyes, the ogress of black eyes who had spoken to him thus.
151.40: "O splendid-faced lady, this pabulum (eatable) prey has been brought by me from KasI for your sake. A second one is standing at the gate. It has been brought to me by providence.
151.41: On hearing the words of the Raksasa that virgin spoke thus: — "O RaksasI, out of his fear for you, your husband utters a lie.
151.42: On hearing these words uttered by the princess, the ogress became extremely infuriated. On seeing the beautiful form (of the princess), she decided that it was the truth. In her anger she hurled words (at her husband).
151.43: She thought thus — ''She has been brought here to be made his wife. Of necessity, this demon will strike a wedge in my head.
151.44: Let there not be any woman in the three worlds who undergoes the misery of having a co-wife. There will hardly be any woman in the three worlds who will survive the harassment due to the misery of being a co-wife.
151.45: After thinking much like this, she spoke these words to her husband, "This girl is mine, as this lady of charming eyes has been brought by you as food for me.
151.46: The maiden of large buttocks spoke to the Brahmana with great pleasure — "Who are you? Whence have you come here? Why do you stay here?
151.47: I ask you this as I am desirous of making you my husband. I am an ogress overcome with pangs of love. I have been abandoned by my husband. I have come here to make you my husband."
151.48: "O Ogress, how can there be the copulation of a RaksasI and a human being? There is no doubt about this that men are remembered as the prey of Raksasas."
151.49: On hearing those words she spoke to him again respectfully — "The impossible is made possible, thanks to the intercession of the Providence.
151.50: The son procreated by a human being will be Ghatotkaca. He will be one who cannot be killed by any other weapon. He will attain death through the weapon called Sakti (of Indra, hurled by Karna against Ghatotkaca).
151.51: Hence, O Brahmana, do not grieve. It is through Providential intercession that I have become your wife. Fate is indeed very powerful.
151.52: O excellent Brahmana, without killing at least one it does not go back to Indra. The person for whose slaying it was hurled will perish even if he be immortal.
151.53: Hence, I shall climb up to the top of this Sala tree, bring the shining Sakti to you and hand it over to you with -a desire for the death of my husband.
151.54: If you do not hit and injure the night-prowler with this Sakti, there is no doubt that the evil-minded one will swallow you as well as me.
151.55: Hence, an enmity (inimical feelings) has been generated in me against my husband of the wicked soul. If he is killed, it will be possible for both of us to have sexual dalliance.

152.3: "O my lover, come on, Enter freely my beautiful cave. Enjoy all the great pleasures, divine as well as human, in my company."
152.4: "So be it" said my husband who was extremely de¬ lighted. Then she took my husband and entered her cave joy¬ fully.
152.5: Without caring to look at the ashes to which her husband's body had been reduced, she clasped my husband with her protruding breasts.
152.6: Men who die therein are never reborn into any womb. Kindly take this lady of bright eyes to her father's house.

153.1: Thus, O lady of beautiful eyebrows, that ogress who had assumed the form of a she-elephant, reached the temple of VisveSa at KLasi within three Muhurtas.
153.2: On reaching that city, the lady of black eyes spoke to her husband — "O Lord, this (city) is glorified as the axe for the cutting of the tree of sin.
153.3: Once Lord Sankara went there to see Pitamaha (god Brahma) the sole creator of all worlds, shining with his own splendour.
153.4: After going there, Mahadeva bowed down to Brahma the preceptor of the worlds. He stood in front of him listening to the recital of the Vedic lore.
153.5: Thereafter, the leader of goblins saw the fifth face of Brahma. On observing him to be impudent and arrogant, he became malicious instantaneously.
153.6: O leading Brahmana, the three-eyed deity, born of anger could not brook his audacity. Hence with the tip of his nail he cut off the head stationed above in the firmament (? )
153.7: O excellent Brahmana, the head of Brahma that had been severed, stuck up to the sproutlike left hand (of Siva). It did not fall off though shaken frequently.
153.8: Brahma became sad. He stood there staring at Siva. Siva became ashamed and he hurriedly went out of the place.
153.9: Though he tried in many ways impatiently to cast off that head, he could not get rid of it. It was a great mystery.
153.10: Being perturbed and worried he remembered Visnu, the Garuda-emblemed deity. The moment he was remembered, Visnu manifested himself.
153.11: O Brahmana, on seeing the omnipresent Visnu the Lord of the chiefs of the Devas, the bull-emblemed deity who had turned pale became humble and bent down his head.
153.12: On seeing (Siva) the antagonist of Brahma, sick and frightened, Hari consoled him and spoke these words that made him satisfied.
153.13: "Inasmuch as the head of Brahma had been cut off, O Sambhu, the omniscient one, you have committed a sin. Experience the fruit thereof for a short while.
153.14: O beloved one, a Karman performed by one, whether auspicious or inauspicious will yield its fruit which one must, of necessity, experience. Even if hundreds of births are to be taken, a Karman does not perish without being experienced.
153.15: What can I do? Where shall I go? On seeing you miserable, O Sambhu, at the sight of your misery, my Pranas are agitated and dispirited.
153.16: This extremely terrible Hatya (the sin of Brahmana- slaughter) emits fish odour; she is senile and sick; she has put out her tongue. O Lord of Devas! She is running after you to catch you.
153.17: Hence you must not stay in any single place for a while. For the sake of your benefit you have to be wander¬ ing (continuously) for twelve years, with the desire for the destruction of sins.
153.18: In order to get rid of the skull he washed his left hand in every sacred water. Wandering thus for three years he reached the penance grove of Badarikasrama.
153.19: O bestower of honour, for the sake of alms he stood at the threshold of Dharmaputra,1 the lord of the Devas and repeatedly said— "Visnu, give me alms."
153.20: On seeing Siva stationed at the threshold, Lord Narayana said— "Take the alms". After saying this he offered his right hand.
153.21: On seeing Hari attempting to give the alms, O excel¬ lent Brahmana, Siva struck his right hand with his trident.
153.22: In the holy centre of Brahma-hrada, he lay immersed in the waters of Brahmahrada. When a period of three years had elapsed he came out with half of his body wounded (?)
153.23: He eulogised Visnu the Lord of the Devas, abiding in the cavity of the heart of everyone, for a long time. Then the Lord of the Universe who was pleased with him granted him the boon.
153.24: "Be victorious, be victorious, O Lord of the universe O Lord Visnu, the storehouse of bliss of the entire universe, knowable only through the' Vedas; O suppressor of demon Madhu, O Nrsimha, O yellow-robed one, O One riding on Garutfa, O Madhava, O primordial Lord.
153.25: O Lord of Rama, the lover of Vrajas, (cowherd's colony), Lord of Radha, Lord of the Devas, the fulfiller of the desires of all, O Krsna, O foremost among the Devas, O ocean of kindness, O destroyer of anguish, O lotus-eyed, O Lord of the greatest beings.
153.26: O Ornament of the family of Yadu, O resident of the milky ocean, O Sauri, O archer, O expert in the art of uplifting the mountain (Govardhana), O deity having a pair of the lotus-feet that destroy the sin of Kali age, O deity who bestow favour on those who eulogise thee, O Kurma (Divine Tortoise), O son of Kasyapa (Vamana).
153.27: O Parasurama — the fire for the forest of wicked kings, O Buddha with a saffron cloth that cleaned off blood from all sacrifices, O Kalkin, O remover of the fear of worldly •existence, O deity governable by (i.e. under the influence of) the devotees, O cowherd, who lift up those who bow •down to you, O Lord of sacred fame and name.
153.28: O remover of the burden of the Earth, O Lord worthy of being worshipped by the enemies of Asuras, O Lord ofPrakrti, O residential abode of the whole universe, O Rama,0 Lord of the mobile and immobile beings shining with many attributes, O Lord who are beyond the three Gunas., O eternal one, O Lord worthy of being worshipped at the head of all, O Lord who protect the enemy of the annihilator Yama through your own people, O Lord with lotus-like feet, O beautiful Padmanabha, O lotus-palmed Lord, O Lord favour¬ ite of the resident of the lotus (i.e. God Brahma), O Lord, worthy of being saluted by the destroyer of Kama and the Lord of three worlds (?)
153.29: O remover of sins, O Lord of the Raghus, O Lord of the Yadavas, one who are fond of Brahmanas, O greater than the greatest one, O Lord worthy of being worshipped by the immortal beings, O wielder of the ploughshare, O remover of sins, O Lord, worthy of being bowed to; O Lord pervaded by the three Gunas, O cleverest one in the three worlds and. three units of Time.
153.30: O Lord with the sole duty of destroying the hosts of demons, O sinless one, O Lord lying on Sesa, the king of serpents, O destroyer of Kariisa, O Lord having the sun and the moon as eyes, O Lord of powerful activities, O Lord hav¬ ing the lustre of fresh clouds, O Lord of the Goddess of Fortune.
153.31: O sacrifice, O Lord maintaining sacrifice, O Lord who were bound with a rope by your mother, O Lord fond of fresh butter, O Lord of groups of cowherd lasses, O destroyer of demons Agha,Baka, Vrsa, Kesin and Putana, O destroyer of Trisiras, Bali and the ten-headed Ravana.
153.32: O destroyer of Naraka and Mura, O Lord who cut off the hands ofBana, O Lord worthy of being worshipped by the enemy of the Tripuras, O.friend of Sudaman, O Lord worthy of being served, O Lord whose lotus-like feet constitute a raft that takes one across the ocean of worldly existence, O Lord whose Aisvarya (Lordship and prowess) is manifest, O ancient one, O One whose arms are full.
153.33: On seeing Hari, Hara fell on the ground like a staff. O leading Brahmana, he got up again and with palms joined in reverence he bowed down to him.
153.34: Visnu spoke to that leader of Bhutas (goblins) who had bowed to him— ' "Choose a boon, I will give it to you. I am pleased with your eulogy."
153.35: On hearing the words of the Lord, Bhutesa, Lord of the goblins who had been harassed by the evil of the slau¬ ghter of a Brahmana spoke this to Hari who is the bestower of worldly pleasures and liberation.
153.36: "O wielder of discus and iron club, I wish to stay in your holy centre since the 'brahmana-slaughter* is seen, stationed outside the limits of your holy centre.
153.37: O Garuda-bannered deity, be merciful to me by the gift of this holy centre. On my going out, the evil of Brahmana- slaughter will harass me again.
153.38: Stationed in your holy centre, I will derive worship in all the three worlds."
153.39: The lover of LaksmI, the daughter of the milk ocean,, said "So be it" and accepted the proposal. O leading Brah¬ mana, ever since then, this place is mentioned as the holy centre pertaining to Siva.
153.40: No sooner did Hara take his holy dip therein, then the skull of Brahma fell down from his hand. That sacred lake became famous by the name of Kapalamocana.
153.41: Bound by the emotional feelings of devotion of Sam- bhu, Visnu is stationed there by the name of Bindu-Madhava after giving his own abode to the Trident-bearing Lord.
153.42: O darling (husband), obstacles are put by the tri¬ dent-bearing Lord (in the lives of people) so that they will serve him. People who are overwhelmed by these obstacles will eulo¬ gise Visnu and then worship Siva.

154.1: When the Brahmana got down, that ogress became once again a beautiful young woman with her face resembling the moon and with plump and protruding breasts.
154.2: On reaching the splendid city of her own father, that virgin spoke to the city governor who had come there in the course of his duty of guarding the exterior limits of the city.
154.3: On hearing the words of the virgin, the city-governor who was well known as Abahu reached the presence of Sudyu¬ mna in a hurry.
154.4: Urged by her, O Lord, I have come to report the matter to you. She says "I am unravaged. May my father inow that I have come back.
154.5: Taking me with him, the demon went to his city beyond the ocean on a mountain full of different kinds of jewels. I was confined in a cave.
154.6: This ogress found that her husband was a defiler of virtue. Moreover, she became enamoured of the hand-
154.7: With her permission give me in marriage to this Brahmana. I shared the same seat with him. Hence he has become my husband.
154.8: "He alone shall be the husband of a woman, with whom she shares the same seat. No one else, so we hear in the Puranas and Agamas.
154.9: I had occupied her back with delight alongwith this Brahmana. Hence, in my opinion he must be my husband, according to Dharma.
154.10: Hence, dear father, console this lady and give me to the Brahmana in accordance with the injunctions in the Agamas and other scriptural texts. I do not wish to choose any other husband."
154.11: On hearing these words of his daughter, Sudyumna the king, consoled the ogress in the form of the lady of slender waist. He stood bowing down with humility.
154.12: "This, my daughter, afraid of losing her merits (Dharma), has sought refuge in you alone. For that reason O chaste woman, your previous husband was killed by you.
154.13: Hence, O gentle lady, she has become one subservient to you. This, my daughter wishes to have as her husband the same gentleman who had been made by you your husband.
154.14: O Ogress, you have been requested by me by means of obeisances and gifts. O lady of beautiful eyes, give your consent to my daughter by extending your help to her.
154.15: At your instance, may my daughter be even the hand-maid of the Brahmana. Eschew the feelings of rivalry common among co-wives and protect my daughter.
154.16: "O excellent king, since you bowed to me with pure feelings, may this lady be the second wife of the Brahmana.
154.17: In the bright half of the month of Phalguna, I must be worshipped in the temple by you alongwith all the citizens.
154.18: Oblations of intoxicating beverages, meat, blood, etc. must be given in the course of worship. If you continue to do in this manner I shall always be the cause of your welfare. O leading king, keep your own words."
154.19: She lovingly spoke to the Brahmana "O excellent Brahmana, make this splendid princess also your wife in the manner laid down in the Grhya texts.
154.20: Then I heard thus — "O gentle lady, your husband
154.21: O blessed lady, in case of woman the riches in¬ herited from parents are fickle and unsteady. It is stated that the riches earned by her husband are permanent.
154.22: He had once been rebuked by you with harsh words. How can you dare to speak to him now? Your entry
154.23: How can he who had been wickedly abandoned by me believe me now." Even as I was thinking thus in my perturbed mind, the palanquin surrounded by kinsmen arrived there. It was tender and elegant. It shone with an umbrella resembling the moon in lustre. Deer skins were spread within it. Stout men bore it on their shoulders.
154.24: O fair-faced lady, we had been sent by your husband immediately after his arrival, to fetch you who have been staying in the house of your parents."
154.25: O gentle lady, on noting that act of my husband I became ashamed. I did not say anything in reply to them. I remained silent.
154.26: O daughter, if the wife does not rejoin her husband when invited (to do so) she is born as a female crow for fifteen births."
154.27: They said thus and assuaged my grief. They took me hurriedly and made me sit in the palanquin with affection, they repeatedly said, 'Go'.
154.28: Thereafter those men placed the palanquin on their shoulders and started immediately with speed. They reached the city of Mahodaya where my husband was staying.
154.29: Thereafter, soon after sunset my husband called me and immediately clasped me within his arms. He made me sit on the couch and kept me within his embrace for a long time.
154.30: Then he called the ogress and the princess and said: ■"Service to this lady's feet should be rendered by both of you with due devotion.
154.31: She had been my wife previously. Hence she is certainly the eldest and senior-most to both of you." Then at the instance of our husband, my feet were touched by those two ladies.

159.1: "O lord of the Devas; O lord of the universe! O lord and preceptor of the mobile and immobile beings Mohini has become unsuccessful like a barren woman in the matter of giving birth (to childern).
159.2: O Kusa-emblemed one the entire world goes to Vaikuntha along the path advocated by Rukmangada. No one comes to me.
159.3: Although the lord of kings entered the body of the discus-bearing lord (Visnu), the mind of all the living beings has not changed.
159.4: O grand-sire of the universe, after observing fast on the day of Visnu, all men including young children, go to the greatest world with their sins dispelled.
159.5: Your daughter, Mohini, the gentle lady is ashamed and has been in swoon. She is not coming near you because she is despised by the world. She does not even take food.
159.6: I have become jobless, what am I to do? Guide me." On hearing the words of Yama the lotus-seated deity said:
159.7: "O fair lady, do not feel aggrieved; you have put in manly efforts. Indeed, there is no question of wounded prestige in regard to the devotees of Visnu.
159.8: O blessed and gentle lady, if the work is begun in earnest and performed assiduously but the fruit is not derived, what is your fault in it now?
159.9: For this reason, O splendid lady, Devas have come as granters of boon. Whether it fructifies or not, one should engage oneself in an activity. One must not remain idle.
159.10: (Defective) the task of heaven-dwellers had been to create the obstacle. Since you have endeavoured with sincerity what is it that the Devas will not do. But O fair- faced lady, along with you, they too have been frustrated by the brilliance of fast which they call the destroyer of obstacles."
159.11: The man who accepts his salary when the ( appoint¬ ed) work is not accomplished, goes definitely to the hell leaving off his master.
159.12: O heaven-dwellers, the servants who do not accom¬ plish the tasks of their masters but still enjoy the salary, are reborn in the Earth as horses.
159.13: I am the destroyer of my husband as well as of my son. I am not successful in accomplishing the task. How can I accept the boon from you, the dwellers of Heaven?"
159.14: O gentle lady, endeavour has been made by you m motivating the king to take food. O gentle lady, when
159.15: O king (Mandhata) 1 When the Devas were speaking thus, the priest of the king (Rukmangada) resplen¬ dent like fire, arrived there.
159.16: The sage who had been engaged in Praniayama, had been living under water. When the twelve-year-period of
159.17: O king (Mandhata), as soon as he came out of water, the actions of MohinI were heard by him. The in¬ furiated prominent sage approached that group of the Devas.
159.18: He condemned all those Devas who were about to grant boons to MohinI. "Fie upon this (woman)? Fie upon this group of Devas! Fie upon this action that should be called a sin.
159.19: She who has killed the son of her husband (and her husband as well) is no better than one who has killed ten thousand persons. She is like a man-eating ogress of the meanst conduct (?). O Devas, even by immolating herself into a well- kindled fire, she cannot gain in purity.
159.20: These three have been considered equal to one- another by the ancient excellent Brahmanas, Viz. Killing ten thousand persons; slaughter of the husband, and the slaughter committed without any purpose. O Devas, even by falling into a well-kindled fire, she cannot purify herself. She had with her nectar-like sweet words deluded Rukmangada, and Dharmarigada. Rukmangada killed his son and attained salvation accompanied by his beloved wife. She (MohinI) has made the Earth bereft of its rulers, the protectors of men.
159.21: She cannot have her residence even in the hells, O Devas. How can she, who is intellectually deficient (and per¬ verse) stay in heaven? O Devas, nor can she stay near the king; she may not attain the eternal region of Visnu.
159.22: Nowhere in the worlds can she have her residence since she has been defiled (and condemned) by the public
159.23: After killing her husband, after taking away the life of her son, after murdering her co-wife who was just like a mother unto her and after destroying the entire Earth, O Devas, what sort of existence or fate will she attain?
159.24: (Defective) O Devas, this lady is a greater sinner (than others). She has destroyed the holy observances of Hari. She always advocated "May food be taken on the day of Hari.55 DownfalL is suffered even by those who take food (to relish it and not) for the sustenance of life. (?)
159.25: If out of ignorance the statement viz-: — "May the food be taken on the day of Hari55 is made, there is an expi¬ ation for it with a hundred Pranayamas.
159.26: O heaven-dwellers, they can atone for it by observing fast on the Ekadasi day, or by taking a bath in the lake Puskara when, the star under which one is born is asso¬ ciated with it (?), or by touching the Deity ( Visriu) in the Boar form or by the worship of God.
159.27: O king (Mandhata), after sayingthis and takingup water in his hand, the eminent Brahmana furiously looked at the daughter of Brahma and violently hurled it on her head. The water then shone like fire.

160.1: Recovering herself from her unconscious senseless condition, Mohini went to the mansions of the Devas, (the Heaven). She was then rebuked by the messenger of the Devas, ctYou are a sinning woman and you have no place here.
160.2: O foolish woman, a habitual sinner, O woman indulging in censuring your own husband, you have no place for staying in the heaven, since you have violated the day of Hari (the Ekadasx Vrata).
160.3: She was taken to hells in the order and made to fall therein. They rebuked her, "O sinful woman, your son Dharmangada had been killed by you through the hands of your husband. Hence experience here the evil effects of the sinful actions perpetrated by you.

161.1: The eight days, remembered in the Agamas (Scrip¬ tures), of the devotees of Visnu as 'Mahadvadasis' are those days wherein Ekadasi is also present. They are observed as the days of fast by the devotees of Visnu.
161.2: In the evening of the previous (i.e. DasamI) day and in the morning of the following ( i.e. Dvadasi) day meal is missed. (Of course, both the meals are eschewed in the middle day i.e. Ekadasi day). But if Ekadasi is overlapped (by the previous Tithi), the observance of full fast is on the next day. The holy rite, in that case, should be performed on the Dvadasi
161.3: Those who are physically incapable of observing full fast can take water, vegetables, fruits, milk or theNaivedya offer¬ ings of Hari. In any case the quantity must not exceed a fourth of the usual diet.
161.4: O chaste lady, the Smartas (those who follow Smrtis) eschew the Ekadasi that is overlapped (by Dasami) at sunrise. Those who are devoid of any desire (from this Vrata) leave off (the Ekadasi) that is overlapped by Dasami even at midnight.
161.5: O splendid lady, thanks to this, even the task of the Devas can be realised. Staying along the border of DaSamI, you will traverse along with the Sun and the Moon too.
161.6: In order to dispel your sins, you move about the various sacred places on the Earth. You can have the benefit of the rite of Ekadasi witliin the period of time between Aruno- daya (dawn) and sunrise.
161.7: If any one observes the holy rite of Ekadasi on the day when it has been occupied by you, he will be the person assisting you, O beloved one of the Devas. The period of two Muhurtas of the dawn should be known ( as your period of occupancy).

161.9: O splendid lady, enjoy the benefit of the merit of those persons who assiduously observe the holy rite of Ekadasi on the day of your occupancy and overlapping. Be gracious unto this Brahmana (? )
161.10: Thus advised and guided by the lotus-seated deity (Brahma) and others, MohinI became much more delighted. She considered her life contented and blessed by the opportu¬ nity to resort to holy centers for wiping off her sins.
161.11: "Although my body had been reduced to ashes, this task of the Devas has been achieved. Although the body is reduced to a mere mass of ashes and consciousness of aerial nature (Linga-Sarira) remains, the path made by the king is swept clean.
161.12: For the delusion of the people, she stationed herself in the transition period of time of Dasami (that is called Surya- vihina (devoid of the Sun or Arunodaya Vedha). She enjoys the whole day (?) in the form of Krcchranta for the downfall into hell of men (? )

161.14: By stationing myself on the border of Yama's Tithi, the universe has been deluded by me. O dear father, thanks to your power, Yama who had been formerly conquered by the king is now made victorious.
161.15: On hearing those words of MohinI, god Brahma the ordainer of the worlds, mollified the Brahmana once again for the sake of his daughter.
161.16: "O deer one, O Vasu, understand this that I speak which is beneficial to this lady. O blessed one, this is conducive to the benefit of all the worlds.
161.17: But she became a sinner inasmuch as she was anta¬ gonistic to Visnu's day. O leading Brahmana may something be done immediately so that she is sanctified."
161.18: On hearing god Brahma's words of request, the sacrificial priest (of Mohini's family) delightfully passed orders for reunion of the physical body (after its creation) with (the jlva) of hisYajya.
161.19: On hearing the words of the Brahmana, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, sprinkled water from his waterpot on the ashes of the body of Mohinl.
161.20: When the ashes were sprinkled with water by Brahma, the maker of the worlds, Mohinl was endowed with a physical body. After bowing down to her father, she humbly bowed down to Vasu, the priest and grasped his feet.
161.21: Then Vasu, the Yajaka (priest) of the king, became joyous. He spoke these words to (Mohinl) who was the wife of his Yajya (one on whose behalf he had to perform a Yajna), whose prowess was wellknown and who had been abandoned by her husband and son.
161.22: Vasu said:- "O gentle lady, anger has been abandon¬ ed by me at the instance of Brahma. I shall facilitate your salvation by means of such rites as visiting holy centres and taking holy dips".
161.23: After saying this to Mohinl, the Brahmana joyously bowed down to Brahma, the lord of the worlds, and the father of Mohinl, and bade goodbye to him.
161.24: Bidden farewell by Mohinl and Vasu out of affection Brahma went to the world beyond darkness through the unmanifest path.

162.1: O MohinI, listen. I shall narrate the characteristics of the holy places severally. On understanding them, the sinners can have the most excellent salvation instantaneously.
162.2: On the surface of the Earth, the most excellent of all the sacred places is the Ganga. There is nothing else which is as destructive of sins as the Ganga.
162.3: On hearing these words of Vasu, her own priest, MohinI who had great respect for a holy dip in the Ganga, bowed to him and said:
162.4: O holy sir, the most excellent Brahmana, now kindly recount the excellent greatness of the Ganga, acknowledged by the Puranas.
162.5: After hearing the unequalled grandeur of the Ganga that is destructive of sins, I shall go alongwith you, to take holy bath in that river that destroys all sins.
162.6: Those lands, countries, mountains and the hermita¬ ges are very holy if the sacred Ganga is ever adjacent to them.
162.7: 5-6, it was in the age of Epics and Puranas that it came to be looked upon as the holiest of rivers. The Mbh and other Puranas are vying with one another in singing the glory of the Ganga (and borrowing such verses from each other). As this section of the NP. deals with pilgrimage to- holy places, it is meet that it should start with the glory of the Gahga.
162.8: A creature (living soul) does not attain by means of austerities, celibacy, Yajnas or renunciation, that state of exis¬ tence or salvation which it may derive after resorting to the Ganga.
162.9: Those men also who commit sins in the early years of their lives but resort to the Ganga during the later years, attain great salvation.
162.11: The man who stands on a single leg for a thousand years (byway of penance), and the man who takes his holy dip into the Ganga for only a month, —these two attain equal benefits.
162.12: By way of penance a man may stand topsy-turvy for ten thousand Yugas. But, if a man stands on the Ganga in any manner as he pleases he is superior to the former.
162.13: In the case of living beings there (in the world), whose minds are afflicted by misery and who are in search of salvation, there is no other place like the Ganga.
162.14: The Ganga may redeem per force those base men who are sinful on account of great and terrible sins. It will prevent them from going to the impure hell.
162.15: In the Krtayuga all sacred places are alike. In the Treta the Puskara lake is the greatest, in the Dvapara Kuru- ksetra is the holiest centre and in the Kali age the Ganga is superior to all other holy places. 1
162.16: In the Kali age, the holy centres and sacred rivers cast off (deposit) their prowess in the Ganga naturally. But the divine Gapga does not cast it off anywhere else.

162.18: The water of the Ganga shall dispel one s sin com¬ mitted till one's death, ifit is used as it is in a holy centre, or if it is taken out elsewhere or if it is taken in hot or cold weather.
162.19: No one has the power to count the gold pieces or the jewels in mount Meru or to describe the extent of the special merits of the waters of the Ganga.
162.20: The same as Mbh. Vana 85.90. Also Kurma I. 27.37 except for Krta-Yuga.
162.21: The drops of waters of the Ganga are superior to many wish-yielding jewels, since they grant the devotees whatever benefit they desire.
162.22: Even if a person gargles once with the waters of the Ganga devoutly, he enjoys in heaven the divine juices originating from the udders of the wish-yielding cow.
162.23: He who sprinkles the Ganga water on the Salagrama stone, shines like the sun that dispels dense darkness at the time of rising.
162.24: He who always partakes of alms sprinkled with the Ganga water, sheds off all sins like the serpent that casts off its slough.
162.25: Heaps of sinful vicious actions as big as the Himalayas or the Vindhya mountains perish through the waters of the Ganga like misfortunes through devotion to Visnu.
162.26: At the very moment when men devoutly enter the Ganga for taking ablution, their sins of Brahmana slaughter etc. cry out 'Alas!' and disappear.
162.27: The man who continuously stays on the banks of the Ganga, and who drinks the water of the Ganga always shall be liberated from the sins accumulated before.
162.28: Verily, he who, resorting to the Ganga, always stays there fearlessly, deserves to be worshipped by gods, mortals and great sages.
162.29: Why should you go in for many Yajnas, words of Japas, austerities and gifts of wealth? For, the Ganga that can be easily served and that bestows heavenly pleasures and salvation is present nearby.
162.30: By means of Yajnas, observances, restraints, charitable gifts and renunciation one does not attain that benefit which one attains by resorting to the Ganga.
162.31: The benefit that a man derives at Prabhasa by giving away a thousand cows when the sun is swallowed byRahu (i.e. at the time of solar eclipse), can be derived by taking bath in the Ganga by a single day.
162.32: In Varanasi particularly, the Ganga bestows liberation immediately. Every month, on the eighth or fourteenth day, it confers emancipation from Samsara.
162.33: The residence on the banks of the Ganga as long as one lives, is the bestower of final beatitude. On the banks of the Ganga, one obtains that benefit and happiness which is usually obtained after performing Krcchra rites or the Candrayana expiation always.
162.34: There is no doubt about this that even after death he will be its devotee and engrossed in devotion. The man who devoutly touches its waters and drinks them, obtains the means of salvation without any strain.
162.35: Just as Indra and other Devas imbibe the nectarine juice present in the moon and the sun, so also men drink the Ganga water through their mouths.
162.36: If one drinks a mouthful of the Ganga water, one attains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice. Salvation is within the grasp of that person who drinks the water of the Ganga freely.
162.37: The water of the Sarasvati becomes stale in three months; that of the Yamuna in seven months, that of the Narmada in ten months and that of the Ganga in a year.
162.38: If in the case of any dead person the obsequies and the water libations are not performed in accordance with the injunctions in the scriptures, they can have the subsequent benefit by casting the bones in the Ganga.
162.39: Of the two—one performing a thousand Candrayana Vratas (vows) subjecting himself to bodily strain and the other drinking the Ganga water as he pleases—it is the latter that excels the former.
162.40: He who drinks water of the Ganga warmed by the rays of the sun gains merits. The drinking of the Ganga water is superior to the partaking of barley grains soaked in cow's urine.
162.41: "O Mohinl listen. I shall recount to you the meritorious benefit of seeing the Ganga as mentioned in the Puranas by sages, the seers of the Truth.
162.42: Just as the serpents become devoid of poison at the sight of Tarksya (Garutfa), so also one is liberated from sins at the sight of the Ganga.
162.43: By seeing, touching and plunging into the Ganga, a man redeems seven subsequent generations, seven earlier generations as well as other manes beyond them.
162.44: By seeing, touching, and drinking the waters of the Ganga and by glorifying the name Ganga, a man sanctifies hundreds and thousands of persons in his family.
162.45: The benefits originating from seeing the Ganga are perfect knowledge, unequalled lordship and prowess, establish¬ ment of auspicious Asramas (stages of life), longevity and renown.
162.46: By the mere sight of the Ganga, all these (the following) perish viz.—the frivolousness of the sense-organs, vices, sins and ruthlessness.
162.47: Violence towards others, crookedness, looking at others' faults etc and the hypocrisy of men, perish by the mere sight of the Ganga.
162.48: If a man wishes for the permanent unchanging region (Moksa) may he see (the Ganga) frequently; may he touch it with devotion again and again.
162.49: By the sight of the Ganga one attains the same merit as one gets elsewhere through the digging and construction of tanks, wells, lakes, watering sheds, asylums, etc.
162.50: By looking at the Ganga with devotional feelings, one attains the same benefit as is obtained in visualizing the great Atman.

162.55: By taking bath into the Ganga and by drinking its water, a man sanctifies up to the seventh generation in his family. He sanctifies seven earlier generations, seven subsequent generations and seven generations beyond these.
162.56: When glorified even casually, the Ganga redeems persons. Even he who carelessly or with lack of faith mentions the name of the holy river Ganga becomes the beneficiary of heavenly pleasures.
162.57: Sins committed on the banks of the Ganga perish as a result of the bath in the Ganga. One gets the merit of a horse-sacrifice by taking bath assiduously in the Ganga by day or by night or during Sandhya (twilight).

163.17: The water of the Sarasvati becomes stale in three months; that of the Yamuna in seven months, that of the Narmada in ten months and that of the Ganga in a year.
163.18: If in the case of any dead person the obsequies and the water libations are not performed in accordance with the injunctions in the scriptures, they can have the subsequent benefit by casting the bones in the Ganga.
163.19: Of the two—one performing a thousand Candrayana Vratas (vows) subjecting himself to bodily strain and the other drinking the Ganga water as he pleases—it is the latter that excels the former.
163.20: He who sees, eulogises and bathes in the Ganga and he who drinks water of the Ganga, attains heavenly pleasures, pure knowledge, Yogic power and salvation.
163.21: He who drinks water of the Ganga warmed by the rays of the sun gains merits. The drinking of the Ganga water is superior to the partaking of barley grains soaked in cow's urine.

164.3: O wife of my Yajya, the benefit obtained by taking bath in the course of the three months (i.e. Magha, Karttika and Vais'akha) is the same as that of the bath in the Ganga water on the Manvadi days and the Yugadi days (i.e. days marking the anniversary of Manvantaras and Yugas).
164.4: The full moon day in the month of Vaisakha is highly meritorious; so also in the months of Karttika and Magha.
164.5: For taking ablutions in the Ganga, rare indeed is the Yoga (specific astronomical period) called Vyatlpata* on the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Magha; sq also is rare the Vaidhrti Yoga **especially on the Kr?nastaml (the eighth day in the dark half of Bhadrapada.)
164.6: If a man takes bath every day at dawn through¬ out the month of Magha in accordance with the injunctions, he shall become Jatismara (one who can recall incidents of the previous births). He shall certainly become perfectly conversant with the scriptural topics and also free from ailments.
164.7: (The devotee must say thus) "O Ganga, I have come on the day of Govinda DvadasI, dispel the multitudes of great sins that I have."

164.12: By worshipping etc. Lord Visnu at the excellent lake (Kusavarla) and god Rudra who abides at Kanakhala or by taking bath into the Ganga at these places, one attains inexhaustible fund of merits.

165.1: Henceforth, the benefit of the rites of taking bath etc. is being explained. O daughter of Brahma and the beloved of the king, listen attentively.
165.2: O gentle lady, if the Sandhya prayers are offered there, the merit thereof is a hundred thousand times more thaa
165.3: If water-libations are offered to the Pitrs by the sons endowed with faith, O MohinI, they give rare and everlasting satisfaction to the manes.
165.4: The Pitrs will stay in the heaven for as many thousand years as the number of gingelly seeds taken by their sons in the holy rite of the Pitrs.
165.5: O auspicious-faced lady, he who wishes his life to be fruitful and has a desire for progeny, must propitiate the Pitrs and the Devas after approaching the Ganga.
165.6: If the Pitrs are propitiated for a month by means of Tarpana 1 rites, and the offerings of balls of rice (Pindas) in the Ganga, all of them are highly delighted and they attain splendour of the sun.
165.7: By offering Arghya even once to the deities alongwith one's own Pitrs, a man shall attain heavenly plea¬ sures in the company of his sons and grandsons.—the Arghya, however, shall consist of special articles of worship alongwith the Ganga water, in a copper vessel of the capacity of a Prastha according to the reckoning in the Magadha land.
165.8: If an excellent man devoutly performs the Japa of eight-syllabled Mantra i.e, Om Namo Narayanaya (Om, obeisance unto Narayana) in the Ganga that bestows bliss on everyone, liberation is within his reach.
165.9: All the Siddhis wait upon the person who observes rules and restraints and performs Japa of the Mantra "Ora namo Narayanaya", for six months.
165.10: He who performs Japa of the Mantra (< Namah Sivaya" (Obeisance to Siva) alongwith the Oihkara, in accor¬ dance with the injunction, for two million and four hundred thousand times, shall become Sankara himself.
165.11: He who worships her continuously even for half a month shall be equal to a.Deva. The benefit will be more if the duration of worship is more.
165.12: O splendid-faced lady, one should worship the divine Ganga, the girdle of the firmament, on that day or on the Aksayatrtlya day or in the month of Vaisakha or Karttika.
165.13: After keeping awake at night, the devotee shall wor¬ ship Visnu, Ganga and Siva with feelings of great devotion, by means of cooked barley grains and gingelly seeds.
165.14: Similarly, the following articles too shall be used in worship viz.—fragrant flowers, saffron, Agallochum, sandal paste, the leaves of TulasI, Bilva etc., the fruits of Matuluhga (citron-likefruit,) etc, incense, lights, Naivedya (food) offer¬ ings etc. Their quantity and variety must be befitting one's affluence and status. He will be going to the world of Visnu, riding on a divine aerial chariot. He will be honoured there for hundreds, thousands and crores of Kalpas.
165.15: Listen to the merit of that person who makes a cha¬ ritable gift of a cow of ghee (?).on the day of Aksaya Trtlya on the banks of the Ganga in accordance with the injunctions.
165.16: Similarly, he who makes a charitable gift of a cow duly, is honoured in the heavenly world for as many years as there are hairs on the body of the cow.
165.17: No doubt need be entertained in this regard that he will enjoy extensive pleasures, that he will be blessed with sons and grandsons and that he will be attaining final emancipation from Samsara.
165.18: He who gives a plot of land on the Ganga, extending to a Nivartana (i.e. about two hundred and ten hands) excels Brahma, Visnu and Siva for as many years as there are particles of dust on that plot of land.
165.19: If anyone gives a village on the bank of the Ganga to Brahmanas, it is conducive to the delight of Brahma, Visnu, Siva, Durga and the sun-god.
165.20: The giver of the village attains thousand times the benefit mentioned in the case of all charitable gifts, all Yajnas, all penances, holy rites and merits. He will be joyously eulogised by the Devas and others. He will be sporting about in an aerial chariot as refulgent as crores of suns in the city pertaining to Visnu (Vaikuntha) or to Sankara (Kailasa). He stays there for as many years as there are dust particles in the plot of land. He is then reborn in the family of Yogins, endow¬ ed with Anima (ability to be atomic in size) and other super¬ normal powers.

166.1: O leading Brahmana, I have been always your devotee. In due order, mention the procedure of the gift of Guqladhenu (a cow made of Jaggery) etc.
166.2: On hearing those words of Mohini, Vasu, her priest, who knew the principles and real meanings of the Vedas and Agamas said smilingly.
166.3: The ground must be smeared with cow-dung, and Kusa grass must be assiduously spread over it. Over it a deer skin measuring four Hastas (hands) must be placed with the neck (portion) directed towards the east.
166.4: The replica of the cow shall be so made that its face is turned towards the East and the calf is near the leg on the northern side (i.e. the left side). In the most excellent Gudadhenu four Bharas (special weight of 3000 Palas) of jag¬ gery must.be used, and the calf is made with a Bhara of Jag¬ gery. The middling replica of the cow is to be. made with two Bharas of jaggery. The calf must be made with half a Bhara of jaggery. The lowest type of Gudadhenu is made of one Bhara of Jaggery (1 Bhara = 200 Palas). The calf shall then be made with a fourth of it. These replicas are made in accordance with the wealth of the household.
166.5: Oyster shells are to be used for their ears. Sugarcane stems for the legs, pure pearls for their eyes; white threads for their sinews and veins and white plants for their dewlaps.
166.6: The knots on their backs shall be represented by a copper pot; the hair by means of white chowries (tail of the antelope called Camara), corals shall be studded to their feet and butter shall represent the udders.
166.7: There must be a bell metal vessel for the purpose of milking into. The pupils of the eyes shall be represented by a sapphire gem; the two horns must be bedecked in gold; the hoofs must be of pure silver.
166.8: "May the Laksmx of all living beings, may goddess Laksml of the Devas stationed in the form of a cow, give me peace and calmness.
166.9: May the beloved wife of Sankara stationed in the bodies of the Rudras, may the goddess in the form of a cow dispel my sin.
166.10: May that Laksml stationed on the chest of Visnu,. may that Laksml in the form of Svaha (wife of the fire god), may the Sakti of the moon, the sun and Indra and which is in the form of the cow be conducive to prosperity.

167.3: The devotee regularly practising Nakta (acceptance •of food after appearance of stars in the evening) shall observe six things viz- partaking of Havisya, ablution, truthfulness, lightness of deity, holy rites in the fire, and sleeping below* (on the bare ground).
167.4: He shall take food in the leafy cups of Palana tree. Conquering the sense-organs, he shall remember Siva. He shall offer separate balls of rice to Dharmaraja and the goddess (Parvati).
167.5: Then he should offer to the extent of his capacity, baked pies cooked in ghee. Taking an Adhaka measure of gin- gelly seeds, he should put it upon the Sivalinga.
167.6: The devotee should worship the lord of all by means of blue lotuses and lilies. If they are not available, he should worship Hara with golden lotuses.
167.7: At the end of a month he should feed eight Brahmanas and give them monetary gifts. For the whole of that month, he should avoid honey (wine) and flesh. He shall observe celi- bacy for the whole of that month.
167.8: Endowed with comely form and good fortune, exer¬ cising royal powers and free from all ailments, he too will enjoy this fruit.
167.9: Or on the fourteenth day, in the bright half of Vais- akha, he who with a concentrated mind observes the Nakta- Vrata should take at night food consisting of cooked Sali rice mixed with milk.
167.10: On the morning of the full-moon day (of Vaisakha) he should duly take bad. in the Gahga. He should perform the Samkalpa rite (formal declaration of the.Mention) for fast. On that night, he should keep awake.
167.11: He goes to Isvara's (god Siva's) palace along- with his ancestors by means of aerial chariots that have the luster of swans and Kunda flowers that resemble the moon* chariots that are yoked with white bulls and embellished with clusters of pearls.
167.12: In the end, he gains detached outlook on life and regains the Ganga. With that faith he courts death in the Gahga. He remembers the previous birth and certainly attains salvation.
167.13: After taking bath in the Gahga with devotion the devotee'should, w.th due formality, offer ten handfuls of black gingelly seeds with ghee into the water. He should also offer balls of ground flour of fried grains as well as those of Jaggery each being ten in number.
167.14: After meditating on the goddess in the water in the manner mentioned before, the devotee should worship her in the objects used for worship (i.e. image or picture). He should observe a special worshipping rite with the following Mantra, (vide verse 66 below).
167.15: During the worship, the ablution of the deity with Paiicamrta is specially recommended. Justin front of the image, the ground shall be scrubbed and smeared with cow-dung.

167.18: After observing all the rites thus, in accordance with the injunction, the devotee should avoid stinginess in the matter of expense. Thereby he is immediately liberated from the ten kinds of sins mentioned below.
167.19: The devotee will be liberated from ten types of sins accumulated in the course of crores of births. There is no doubt about itsofar as the utterance of Brahma goes.
167.20: (The Ganga) worshipped with the following Mantra does redeem from worldly existence, forty earlier generations and forty subsequent generations.
167.21: The following hymn should be taken up for repeti¬ tion on that day. The devotee should, thereafter, proceed ahead with the worship of Visnu.
167.22: Om obeisance to Siva, the Ganga, the bestower of auspicious things. Obeisance be to you. Hail be to the deity of the form of Visnu. Obeisance, Obeisance be to you the Ganga.
167.23: Bow to the deity, the embodiment ofallDevas; obeisance to the deity of the form of medicine; Hail to you, O most excellent physician of all ailments of everyone.
167.24: Obeisance be to you; O queller of poisons origi¬ nating from mobile and immobile beings; obeisance, obeisance to the destroyer of the poison of worldly existence; obeisance to the enlivener.
167.25: Repeated bows to the remover of the three types of miseries of human beings, to the Is'varl (controller) of vital breaths. Obeisance to you, the remover of distress, the bestower of calmness and peace; obeisance to you the omniformed one.
167.26: Hail to the purifier of all for liberation from sins; obeisance to the deity bestowing worldly pleasures and salvation, obeisance, obeisance to the deity possessing pleasures.
167.27: Bow to you, the Mandakini (i.e. heavenly Ganga); obeisance, obeisance to the bestower of heavenly pleasures; obeisance to the embodied form of the set of the three worlds; obeisance, obeisance to the divine one.
167.28: Hail to you stationed in Sukla (i.e. Siva); obeisance, obeisance to the possessor of well-being; Bow to you the divinity stationed in the seats of the Devas. Hail to you the possessor of brilliance.
167.29: Salutations to the slow-moving river, to the bearer of the Linga, to Narayanl. Obeisance to you who are friendly to the universe. Obeisance to you, O Revatl.
167.30: Obeisance always to you of huge size. Salutations to the support of all the worlds. Obeisance to you the chief one in the universe. Repeated bow to you NandinI (the delighter).
167.31: Obeisance to the large one, the auspicious one and to the immoral one; salutations to the Pure one, devoid of dust (sin); obeisance to the deity whose access is both far and near. Obeisance, obeisance to the redeeming divinity.
167.32: Obeisance to you who abide in the heaven; salutations to the non-different, to the unsplit divinity* Obeisance to the quiescent one; bow to you the stable found¬ ation; obeisance, obeisance to you the bestower of these boons.
167.33: Obeisance to the fierce one. Obeisance to one who prattles with her mouth (?); salutations to the enlivener; obeisance to one who goes to the Brahman; obeisance to one who bestows the Brahman; obeisance, obeisance to the destroyer of sins.
167.34: Bow to the queller of the anguish of those who bow down; salutations to the mother of the universe; obeisance to Vilusa (one who injures (the wicked); obeisance to the remover of difficulties; repeated obeisance to the efficient one.
167.35: You alone are the primordial Prakrti; you are lord Narayana. O Ganga, you are the great Atman; you are Siva. Obeisance, obeisance to you."
167.36: O daughter of Brahma, those men who leave off their vital breaths by casting their bodies into the Ganga go to the world of Visnu eulogised by those who are domiciled in the heaven.
167.37: (?) He who dies pariially due to observance of fast and partially due to being drowned in the Ganga, is not reborn. He attains Sayujya (identity) with the Brahman.
167.38: The embodied being that casts off its vital breaths (dies by throwing himself) in the Ganga has the same salvation as that of an intelligent being endowed with Sattva guna and Yogic practice.
167.39: The NP, though a Vaisnava Purana, always advocates the one¬ ness between Siva and Visnu and other deities. He emphasizes ekam sat (Reality is one).
167.40: The man who takes up the vow of abstaining from taking food and dies on the banks of the Ganga, attains in fact the greatest world alongwith the Pitrs (his ancestors).
167.41: Those intelligent men (self-possessed ones) by whom the physical body is cast off after going off to the Ganga attain equality with the Devas. Hence, one shall reasoningly eschew all other means of bestowing liberation and resort to the Ganga till one's body falls.
167.42: He who dies in the firmament on the Earth or in the water, attains the everlasting region worthy of being honoured by Brahma, Visnu and Siva.
167.43: Wherever one may die, if one devoutly remembers the Ganga when death is imminent, one goes to the city per¬ taining to Siva or to Visnu.
167.44: The Ganga came out of the cluster of the matted hair of Sambhu, that is very rough and hard. It flowed over the sons of Sagara who were sinners and led them to the heaven.
167.45: A man's stay in the heavenly world begins from the moment when his bones are cast off into the waters of the Ganga by other men.
167.46: If any one's bones are cast off into the Ganga water within the ten days (from his death), he attains a benefit similar to that of the death within the Ganga.
167.47: The same as Matsya 106.52, Kuma,1. 37.32; NP Supra I.
167.48: O excessively blessed lady, the space of three Yojanas on either side of the Ganga should be known as Siddha- ksetra. It was here that Rama and Sambhu had their penance groves.
167.49: No man shall accept Pratigraha (monetary gift) in a holy centre or in the sacred temples. A man shall abstain from it under all circumstances (i.e. even when there are justifiable reasons).
167.50: O gentle lady, by selling the Ganga, one becomes (guilty) of selling (god) Visnu. When Janardana is sold, all the three worlds are sold.
167.51: He who applies the clay taken up from the banks of the Ganga on his head assumes the form of the sun for the destruction of darkness.
167.52: A man shall spread the dust particles taken from the banks of the Ganga and place the balls of rice for his Pitis. He shall thus propitiate them and lead them to heaven.
167.53: O gentle lady, thus the excellent greatness of the Ganga has been recounted to you. A man who reads this or listens to this attains the greatest region of Visnu.
